known.title: Acceptance A1 checks only that the two skills name plan:drafting, which the old four-label line already does, so it passes when step 1 is not done
known.locator: Acceptance, row A1 (line 30); Steps, row 1 reword_blocks (line 23)
known.summary: A1 runs `grep -q "plan:drafting"` on security/SKILL.md and refactor/SKILL.md and expects exit 0 as the proof that the reworded blocks name the creation label. At repo_ref both files already hold `plan:drafting | plan:planned | plan:ongoing | plan:blocked` (security/SKILL.md line 79, refactor/SKILL.md line 78), so the command exits 0 before any change, and with `-q` it exits 0 when only one file matches. A2 runs the docks gate, which checks no record-block text. So no Acceptance row fails when step 1 leaves the old enumeration in place; a row must check the new wording, or the absence of the old line.

known.title: The plan keeps the old four-label line as a legacy line for one release and schedules its removal in a follow-up plan, a temporary fix that the user did not ask for
known.locator: Research, consumers bullet (line 14); Steps, row 1 reword_blocks (line 23)
known.summary: The consumers bullet keeps the old line under the new wording as a `legacy:` line for one release, and a follow-up plan removes the three lines after the next docks release; step 1 adds them. At repo_ref, plan-contract.md (Body section, line 106) says that temporary fixes, workarounds, and solutions that schedule future maintenance are prohibited unless the user explicitly asked for a temporary fix and the plan records that request in Goal or Open questions, and that reviewers treat an unrequested temporary fix as a goal_fit finding. The Goal asks for the reword instead of the enumeration and records no such request, and the legacy line keeps the enumeration that the Goal removes. The bullet also names no reader of the old line in the repository.

known.title: Research says that skill-agent-pipeline enumerates the four phase labels, but its record block already describes creation state, so step 1 rewrites a correct block of a third skill
known.locator: Research, skill-agent-pipeline bullet (line 12); Steps, row 1 reword_blocks, Files and Done when (line 23); Steps, row 2 hash_gate, Files (line 24)
known.summary: The bullet says that the record block of plugins/docks/skills/productivity/skill-agent-pipeline/SKILL.md (lines 75-77) holds `plan:drafting | plan:planned | plan:ongoing | plan:blocked`, so step 1 rewords it too and adds a legacy line there. At repo_ref that block (line 76) reads `GitHub issue #<n> labeled plan, plan:drafting (created and managed by plan-manager)`: it already states creation state and manager ownership, and no file other than security/SKILL.md and refactor/SKILL.md holds the four-label line. So step 1 and step 2 change a third skill and its content hash without cause, and the legacy line would add an enumeration that this skill never had.
